# shikigami

TypeScript Agent SDK with hexagonal architecture — core defines ports, adapters are injected.

## Quickstart

Get a working agent in under 30 minutes.

```bash
npm install shikigami @shikigami/kairo
```

Set your API key (works with any OpenAI-compatible provider — Groq, Together, OpenRouter, local):

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
# Optional: export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1"
```

```ts
import { Agent } from 'shikigami';
import { MemoryManagerImpl } from 'shikigami/retrieval';
import { SimpleStore } from 'shikigami/kairo/memory'; // or from '@shikigami/kairo/memory'

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    memoryManager: new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new SimpleStore()] }),
  },
});

const result = await agent.execute('What is the capital of France?');
if (result.ok) {
  console.log(result.data);  // "The capital of France is Paris."
} else {
  console.error(result.error);
}
```

> **OPENAI_API_KEY** and **OPENAI_BASE_URL** are read automatically from environment variables if present, or you can pass `apiKey` and `baseUrl` / `baseURL` directly in `agentConfig`.

---

## Memory (retrieval-order rule)

Plug in memory via `MemoryManagerImpl` (a well-known tool). Core ships only the interface — bring your own `MemoryStrategy` implementations (e.g. a Kairo template like `SimpleStore`).

```ts
import { MemoryManagerImpl } from 'shikigami/retrieval';
import { SimpleStore } from '@shikigami/kairo/memory';

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    memoryManager: new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new SimpleStore()] }),
  },
});
```

The agent follows the **retrieval-order rule** (memory first → tools → explicit unknown):

- `memoryManager.retrieve({ query, correlationId })` runs at the start of every `execute()`.
- `memoryManager.store({ query, result, correlationId })` runs after each task and after the final response.
- On a memory miss, the prompt includes an explicit-unknown instruction (swappable via `AgentConfig.memoryInstructionTemplate`, default `DEFAULT_MEMORY_INSTRUCTION`).

**Swap-by-replacement (FR-14):** swapping memory is a one-line change — no agent code touched.

```ts
// before
new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new SimpleStore()] })
// after — swap in a vector store by changing one line
new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new VectorStore()] })
```

> **Note:** `MemoryManager` exported from `shikigami/retrieval` is an **interface type** (not constructable). The class is `MemoryManagerImpl`.

## Sessions (conversation continuity)

Wire a `Session` port to persist conversation history and task position across calls. Core defines the contract; implementations are Kairo templates (Epic 7) — a stub satisfies it in tests.

```ts
const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    session: mySessionTemplate,
  },
});
```

- Prior turns are carried forward without re-supplying.
- An interrupted run resumes at the last uncompleted task (`pendingTask` in session state).
- Session failures are non-fatal — the run continues (surfaced via the `ERROR` event).

## Tools (creation contract & pipeline)

Build custom tools with the creation contract — `(action, inputParser, outputParser, [inputInterceptors], [outputInterceptors])` — via `createTool`. A missing required slot fails loudly at creation.

```ts
import { createTool, ToolExecutor } from 'shikigami/tools';

const sum = createTool({
  name: 'sum',
  description: 'adds 1 to the input',
  inputParser: { parse: (i) => Number(i), serialize: (o) => o },
  outputParser: { parse: (i) => i, serialize: (o) => `result:${o}` },
  action: async (input) => ({ result: (input as number) + 1 }),
});

const context = { correlationId: 'demo', agentConfig: {} };
const out = await new ToolExecutor().execute(sum, '41', context);
// out.result === 'result:42'
```

Tool calls execute in a **fixed pipeline order** (FR-24): input interceptor → input parser → action → output parser → output interceptor → output validator. Cross-tool execution is sequential in v1.

Method convention: `inputParser.parse` runs on the way in, `outputParser.serialize` on the way out (the other method on each parser is unused by the pipeline), and `outputParser.serialize` must return a `ToolOutput`-shaped value.

- **Interceptors** are block/allow guards (hit-run exactly once on block, FR-25).
- **`ToolOutputValidator`** runs last; the default is passthrough — validation is opt-in (AR-17). Parser/validator failures surface as typed `ToolError`.
- **`ToolRegistry`** registers tools by name and looks them up (`TOOL_NOT_FOUND` on a miss).
- **Agents invoke configured tools** (`agentConfig.tools`) through this pipeline via a prompt-level protocol: the model responds with a `TOOL_CALL:` line + JSON, the agent runs the tool through `ToolExecutor` and feeds the result back as a `role: 'tool'` message — bounded by `maxToolCallsPerTask` (default 3). Tool failures are non-fatal; a malformed invocation is treated as a plain-text answer. On loop-budget exhaustion the task result is an explicit marker string (`Tool loop limit of N reached...`) rather than an error envelope. Sub-agent tool interceptor blocks do not invoke the parent's `hitRun` (hitRun is a parent-run concern, consistent with the guardrail-bypass limitation).
- **Native function calling (opt-in):** set `toolCallingMode: 'native'` to use OpenAI-compatible `tools`/`tool_calls` instead of the prompt-level protocol. Add an optional `inputSchema` (JSON Schema) to `createTool` so the model knows the input shape; absent schemas default to `{ type: 'object' }` and the `inputParser` remains the runtime validator (core adds no schema-validation dependency). Native mode requires an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Groq, Together, OpenRouter, most local servers); streaming tool calls are not yet supported — native mode uses non-streaming calls.

## Streaming & Events (opt-in)

Attach listeners via `agent.addListener(EventType.STREAM, fn)` to consume token/execution streaming, metrics, and errors as they happen. Events are **async-buffered** — no real-time delivery guarantees in v1 (FR-47). Each event carries a `correlationId` (run id) and a monotonic `sequenceNumber` within that run's scope; filter by correlation ID to reconstruct causal order (AR-19). STREAM and METRICS listeners are fully separate — a STREAM listener is never invoked by a METRICS emission and vice versa, and event data never contains API keys or sensitive data.

```ts
import { EventType } from 'shikigami';

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: { model: 'gpt-4o', streaming: true },
});
const unsub = agent.addListener(EventType.STREAM, (event) => {
  const token = (event.data as { token: string }).token;
  process.stdout.write(token);
});

await agent.execute('Tell me a story');
unsub(); // stop listening
```

- **Opt-in flag:** set `streaming: true` on `AgentConfig` (or per-run via `execute(task, { streaming: true })`); default `false` keeps the common run byte-identical (NFR-10). Sub-agents inherit the flag through config inheritance.
- **What streams:** the user-facing answer LLM calls (the task answer and the multi-result merge). Internal probes (`understand`, failure decisions, tool-loop iterations) are not streamed — with an active tool loop, streaming applies to the non-tool-loop answer path only (documented v1 limitation).
- `execute()` still returns the full assembled response in the envelope — streaming is additive, it does not change the public verb surface (AR-3).

**Block/error telemetry (Story 8.3):** when a guardrail or tool interceptor blocks, or an agent error is caught (task failure, reasoning failure, sub-agent abort, orchestration error), the run emits an `ERROR` event (`{ message, source, code }`) and a `METRICS` event (`{ kind: 'block' | 'error', source, code }`) at the catch point. Filter `METRICS` by `kind` to tell telemetry from the run-summary event — a run can emit both. Known limitation: telemetry cannot distinguish a guardrail block from a guardrail failure beyond the error `code` (PRD §4.2).

**Token usage (Story 8.2):** every run's final `METRICS` event carries an aggregate `usage` field (`{ prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens }`) summed across that run's LLM calls — usage only, never cost (NFR-8). Sub-agents track usage on their own run scope; the parent's `METRICS` reflects the parent's own calls. Streamed runs request usage via the standard `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` parameter; if the provider ignores it, the streamed contribution is simply zero. Strict servers that reject the field are handled with a transparent one-time retry without it, so streaming keeps working (NFR-10).

## Kairo Templates (batteries included)

Install the companion adapter package and wire the four launch templates with **import-and-inject** — no boilerplate, and every template is swappable via one-line instantiation (swap-by-replacement).

```ts
import { Agent } from 'shikigami';
import { MemoryManagerImpl } from 'shikigami/retrieval';
import { ReasoningManager } from 'shikigami/reasoning';
import { SimpleStore } from '@shikigami/kairo/memory';
import { WebSearchTool } from '@shikigami/kairo/tools';
import { SimpleReasoningStrategy } from '@shikigami/kairo/reasoning';
import { SimpleInputGuardrail } from '@shikigami/kairo/guardrails';

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    memoryManager: new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new SimpleStore()] }),
    tools: [new WebSearchTool({ search: mySearchImpl })],
    reasoningManager: new ReasoningManager({ strategies: [new SimpleReasoningStrategy()] }),
    guardrails: [new SimpleInputGuardrail({ blockedTerms: ['politics'] })],
  },
});
```

- **`SimpleStore`** (`@shikigami/kairo/memory`) — in-memory `MemoryStrategy`: stores entries in an internal array; retrieve returns the entire array (no selective retrieval, embedding search, or ranking — FR-16a).
- **`WebSearchTool`** (`@shikigami/kairo/tools`) — a `Tool` built via the creation contract (`createTool`): inject your own `search` implementation; without one it returns a deterministic placeholder (offline, no API key).
- **`SimpleReasoningStrategy`** (`@shikigami/kairo/reasoning`) — deterministic `ReasoningStrategy` that synthesizes the context; wire it into `ReasoningManager`.
- **`SimpleInputGuardrail`** (`@shikigami/kairo/guardrails`) — block/allow-only `Guardrail` with configurable blocked terms; it never transforms the prompt (FR-29).

**Swap-by-replacement — all components in one line:**

```ts
// Swap memory: array store → vector store
new MemoryManagerImpl({ strategies: [new VectorStore()] })

// Swap reasoning strategy: simple → step-back or custom
new ReasoningManager({ strategies: [new StepBackStrategy()], reviewer: new ConfidenceReviewer() })

// Swap guardrail: simple blocked-terms → custom ML-based
new SimpleInputGuardrail({ blockedTerms: [] })   // before
new MyMlGuardrail({ endpoint: 'http://...' })    // after — one line, no agent code change
```

> Note: the memory-manager *class* is exported from `shikigami/retrieval` as `MemoryManagerImpl` (`MemoryManager` is the interface type).

## Reasoning & Quality Gate

Wire a `ReasoningManager` into the agent to add a reasoning step before acting. The manager runs configured strategies in parallel, aggregates outputs, and applies a reviewer-agent quality gate (threshold 0.9 by default).

```ts
import { ReasoningManager, LlmReviewer, ConfidenceReviewer } from 'shikigami/reasoning';
import { SimpleReasoningStrategy } from '@shikigami/kairo/reasoning';

const reasoningManager = new ReasoningManager({
  strategies: [new SimpleReasoningStrategy()],
  // Use LlmReviewer for production; ConfidenceReviewer for offline/testing
  reviewer: new ConfidenceReviewer(),
  threshold: 0.9,           // quality gate (default: 0.9)
  effortLevel: 'HIGH',      // LOW: 3 retries, HIGH: 5, ULTRA: 10 (default: HIGH)
});

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    reasoningManager,
  },
});
```

- **`LlmReviewer`** — uses an LLM call to rate reasoning quality 1–10. For production use. Requires `apiKey` in config.
- **`ConfidenceReviewer`** — derives a score from the result's `confidence` field — no LLM call; offline-safe. Ideal for testing.
- **Effort levels:** `LOW` = 3 retries, `HIGH` = 5 retries (default), `ULTRA` = 10 retries.
- **Exit-on-max:** if the threshold is not met after all retries, the best-rated result is returned (never silently dropped).
- **Swap-by-replacement:** switching reasoning strategies = one-line instantiation change.

## Guardrails

Wire guardrails to block undesired prompts before the agent runs. Guardrails are block/allow only — they never transform the prompt.

```ts
import { Agent } from 'shikigami';
import { SimpleInputGuardrail } from '@shikigami/kairo/guardrails';

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    guardrails: [new SimpleInputGuardrail({ blockedTerms: ['spam', 'violence'] })],
    hitRun: (err) => {
      // Invoked once on block — log, audit, or alert here
      console.error('Guardrail blocked:', err.code, err.message);
    },
  },
});
```

- **`SimpleInputGuardrail`** blocks any prompt containing a configured term (case-insensitive substring match).
- **`hitRun`** (in `AgentConfig`) is invoked exactly once when a guardrail blocks or a tool interceptor blocks. It is synchronous — if it throws, the error is unhandled (developer's fault).
- **Composition:** the SDK accepts any single `Guardrail` object, including composed ones — chain or parallelize in your layer.
- **Known limitation:** guardrails run on every `execute()` call (including `invokeAgent` / `delegate`, which call `execute()` on the same agent). Sub-agents spawned via the Watchdog bypass the parent's guardrail gate.

## Sub-agent Delegation & Watchdog

The agent can spawn sub-agents to parallelize work. The `Watchdog` bounds and monitors sub-agent lifecycle; `TaskManager` manages the linear task list.

```ts
import { Agent } from 'shikigami';

const agent = new Agent({
  agentConfig: {
    model: 'gpt-4o',
    watchdog: {
      maxConcurrent: 3,    // max concurrent sub-agents (default: 5)
      maxDepth: 2,         // max delegation depth (default: 3)
      timeoutMs: 300_000,  // sub-agent timeout in ms (default: 600_000 = 10 min)
    },
    maxSubAgentRetries: 1, // retries per failed sub-agent (default: 1)
  },
});

// Spawn a sub-agent inline:
const result = await agent.execute(
  'Research climate change causes and effects, then draft a 3-paragraph summary.'
);
// The agent internally breaks this into tasks and may delegate sub-tasks
```

- **`Watchdog`** monitors lifecycle only — never creates tasks. The Orchestrator creates tasks; `Watchdog` spawns, monitors, and times out sub-agents.
- **Bounds (AD-6):** max 5 concurrent per parent, max depth 3 levels, default 10-minute timeout.
- **Failure handling:** sub-agent failures are non-fatal; the parent decides retry/abort/continue via `hitRun`.
- **Task lifecycle:** `TaskManager` maintains a linear pending-task queue (`createTask`, `nextPendingTask`). Only the Orchestrator may advance task state.
- **`invokeAgent(goal, config?)`** and **`delegate(goal, config?)`** are convenience verbs that call `execute()` on the same agent (guardrailed) or spawn a sub-agent depending on the implementation path.

```ts
// Direct access to Watchdog/TaskManager (advanced use):
import { Watchdog, TaskManager } from 'shikigami/delegation';

const watchdog = new Watchdog(
  { maxConcurrent: 5, maxDepth: 3, timeoutMs: 600_000 },
  (taskId) => taskManager.getTaskStatus(taskId), // optional: pre-restart status check
);
const taskManager = new TaskManager();
```

## Error Taxonomy

All errors extend `ShikigamiError` and carry a `code: ErrorCode` and optional `context: Record<string, unknown>`.

```ts
import { ShikigamiError, GuardrailError, ToolError, ErrorCode } from 'shikigami';

const result = await agent.execute('...');
if (!result.ok) {
  const err = result.error;
  if (err instanceof GuardrailError && err.code === ErrorCode.GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED) {
    console.log('Blocked:', err.message, err.context);
  }
}
```

| Error class | Module | Key `ErrorCode` values |
|---|---|---|
| `GuardrailError` | guardrails | `GUARDRAIL_BLOCKED`, `GUARDRAIL_FAILED` |
| `InterceptorError` | tools | `INTERCEPTOR_BLOCKED`, `INTERCEPTOR_FAILED` |
| `ToolError` | tools | `TOOL_EXECUTION_FAILED`, `TOOL_NOT_FOUND`, `TOOL_CREATION_FAILED` |
| `WatchdogError` | delegation | `WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`, `WATCHDOG_CONCURRENCY_EXCEEDED`, `WATCHDOG_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` |
| `ReasoningError` | reasoning | `REASONING_FAILED`, `REASONING_QUALITY_BELOW_THRESHOLD` |
| `MemoryError` | retrieval | `MEMORY_STORE_FAILED`, `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_FAILED` |
| `SessionError` | session | `SESSION_FAILED` |
| `OrchestrationError` | core | `LOOP_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED`, `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_OPEN` |

All errors are also importable from their module subpaths (e.g., `import { GuardrailError } from 'shikigami/guardrails'`).

## API Quick Reference

### `shikigami` (core)

| Export | Kind | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `Agent` | class | Main orchestrator entry point. Constructor: `{ agentConfig: AgentConfig, subAgentConfig?: SubAgentConfig }`. Public methods: `execute(task, options?)`, `addListener(type, fn)`, `storeKnowledge(entry)`, `retrieveKnowledge(query)`, `invokeAgent(goal, config?)`, `delegate(goal, config?)`. |
| `AgentConfig` | interface | Constructor options. Key fields: `apiKey`, `baseUrl` (or `baseURL`), `model`, `temperature`, `maxTokens`, `systemPrompt`, `memoryManager`, `tools`, `maxToolCallsPerTask`, `toolCallingMode` (`'prompt'|'native'`), `streaming`, `guardrails`, `reasoningManager`, `session`, `hitRun`, `watchdog`, `maxSubAgentRetries`. |
| `AgentRunOptions` | interface | Per-run overrides for `execute()`. Fields: `model`, `temperature`, `maxTokens`, `systemPrompt`, `streaming`. |
| `LlmClient` | class | Thin fetch-based OpenAI-compatible client. Constructor: `{ apiKey, baseURL?, model? }`. Methods: `chat(request)`, `chatStream(request)`. |
| `LlmMessage` | interface | Chat message. Fields: `role: 'system'|'user'|'assistant'|'tool'`, `content: string \| null` (nullable for native tool-call assistant responses), `name?`, `tool_call_id?`, `tool_calls?`. |
| `LlmRequest` | interface | LLM API request. Fields: `model`, `messages`, `temperature?`, `max_tokens?`, `stream?`, `tools?`, `tool_choice?`. |
| `LlmResponse` | interface | LLM API response. |
| `LlmUsage` | interface | Token usage. Fields: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`. |
| `LlmClientConfig` | interface | LlmClient constructor config. Fields: `apiKey`, `baseURL?`, `model?`, `temperature?`, `maxTokens?`. |
| `ApiEnvelope<T>` | type | `ApiSuccess<T> \| ApiFailure`. Returned by `execute()` as `ApiEnvelope<string>`. |
| `ApiSuccess<T>` | type | `{ ok: true; data: T }` |
| `ApiFailure` | type | `{ ok: false; error: Error }` |
| `EventType` | enum | Event kinds: `STREAM`, `METRICS`, `ERROR`, `TASK_CREATED`, `TASK_STARTED`, `TASK_COMPLETED`, `TASK_FAILED`, `SUBAGENT_SPAWNED`, `SUBAGENT_COMPLETED`, `SUBAGENT_FAILED`. |
| `ShikigamiEvent` | interface | Base event shape. Fields: `correlationId`, `sequenceNumber`, `type`, `timestamp`, `data`. |
| `EventListener` | type | `(event: ShikigamiEvent) => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `ErrorCode` | enum | All typed error codes across modules (see Error Taxonomy table above). |
| `ShikigamiError` | class | Base error class. Fields: `code: ErrorCode`, `message`, `context?: Record<string, unknown>`. |
| `GuardrailError` | class | Thrown on guardrail block/failure. |
| `InterceptorError` | class | Thrown on interceptor block/failure. |
| `ToolError` | class | Thrown on tool execution/creation failure. |
| `WatchdogError` | class | Thrown on watchdog timeout/concurrency/depth violation. |
| `ReasoningError` | class | Thrown on reasoning failure or below-threshold result. |
| `MemoryError` | class | Thrown on memory store/retrieve failure. |
| `SessionError` | class | Thrown on session failure. |
| `OrchestrationError` | class | Thrown on orchestration failures (timeout, max retries, circuit breaker). |

## Known Limitations

- **Guardrails run on every `execute()` call.** `invokeAgent` / `delegate` are aliases that call `execute()` on the same agent, so the guardrail gate applies to those prompts too. The spec'd known limitation — that prompts of separately spawned sub-agents (via the Watchdog, Epic 4) bypass the guardrail layer — applies only once distinct sub-agent instances exist. Until then, treat every prompt submitted through this agent as guardrailed.
- **Streaming tool calls not supported in native mode.** `toolCallingMode: 'native'` uses non-streaming calls; set `streaming: false` (or omit) when using native tool calling.
- **No Anthropic adapter in v1.** Core uses native `fetch` for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Anthropic requires a post-v1 adapter.
- **`LlmMessage.content` is `string | null`.** Assistant messages carrying `tool_calls` have `null` content. Handle the nullable when reading message content directly.
- **Sub-agent guardrail bypass.** Separately spawned sub-agent instances (via Watchdog) bypass the parent agent's guardrail layer. This is by spec — sub-agents run in their own execution context.
